There are ablative and nonablative CO2 laser treatments:

     Ablative CO2 laser treatments use a beam of light to remove the outer layers of the skin, revealing smoother, fresher skin beneath, while also heating deeper layers to stimulate collagen production.   This helps tighten and firm the skin over time. The treatment can be quite intense and likely requires general anesthesia, especially for deeper procedures.   Recovery time can require two weeks or more, but the skin can remain red for several weeks or longer. 
      Nonablative lasers are gentler and allow for quicker recovery. Most nonablative lasers are fractional. This treatment uses a beam of light (laser), divided into thousands of microscopic pixels, and is delivered by a device to treat a small fraction of the skin at a time without damaging the skin's top layer.  There are no serious side effects; typically redness and swelling lasting two days. During the healing process new cells are generated improving skin texture and tone. This type of treatment gets rid of fine lines, age spots, enlarged pores and smoothes textured skin.  Results are achieved with little discomfort and minimal risk, usually after a series of 3-5 treatments, with one treatment every 3-8 weeks.  Downtime is minimal, only a few days at most. It delivers powerful results without the harsh side effects or the high risk of complications posed by ablative laser therapy. This treatment is safe for all skin types.
     If you're considering laser therapy, consult a dermatologist about which option is recommended.

There are a few things you can do to manage an oily scalp. First you can make sure you are eating a healthy balanced diet. This will promote your body's production of healthy skin cells. In addition, you should make sure your diet consists of foods rich in omega-3 fatty acids, proteins, and vitamin A to maintain the health of your hair. Salmon and flax seeds are a great source of these nutrients. Surprisingly, dehydration can also lead to an oily scalp so it is important to drink enough water throughout the day.

You also want to make sure you limit handling and styling your hair. The heat and tension used with curling wands and straightening irons can cause drying and damage the scalp, making the sebaceous glands react by producing even more oil. Brush or comb your hair gently and briefly and try to avoid contact with your scalp. this limits the transfer of oil from the scalp to the hair shafts. Also try not to touch your hair. Instead of cutting it you might want to leave it longer so you can wear it up and out of reach.

Hair hygiene is vital when you have an oily scalp. Since your pillow case is accumulating the oil, dirt and sweat from your hair everyday it is very important to change your pillow case weekly.

If the chain is too short, this shift is difficult to make, and the derailleur cage is stretched out and almost parallel to the chainstay. A more precise method includes removing your current chain.   Once the chain has been removed, shift the front derailleur to the largest chainring, and the rear to the smallest. Wrap the chain around the largest chainring (at the rear), making that if the chain has an outer plate, it is routed toward the front chainring.  Pass the chain through the front derailleur cage and onto the largest front chainring, Hold chain at the 5 o’clock position.  If you are using a masterlink chain, install half the mater link onto the front end of the chain to account for the extra half link the master link provides.

Your perfect saddle depends on your body and cycling habits. Core strength, posture, where you cycle, your pelvis width, and your bone structure all determine which saddle will be the most comfortable for you. You should make sure the shape of the saddle conforms to your anatomy, that it gives you good balance and does not exert undo pressure or friction on your thighs, perineum, and glutes. The saddle should not be too narrow nor too wide. Extra wide saddles also are available for cyclists that maybe a bit overweight. Although unusual for mountain bikes, since you have had back problems you might consider a kick-up on the back of the saddle that prevents you from sliding while climbing and supports your lower back while pedaling. 

Besides bike saddles, the wheels, the curb front fork and the seat post suspension all play a role in reducing the shock from bumps and can make your bike ride much more comfortable.
